claims.statement: main.py is the FastAPI app entrypoint: it defines the /varieties, /products, /batches, /scan, and /deduct endpoints, implements FIFO/expiry-ordered stock deduction for both weight and unit tracking, and serves the built frontend via app.frontend().
database.py constructs the SQLAlchemy engine and SessionLocal from the DATABASE_URL environment variable (loaded via dotenv) and exposes get_db as the FastAPI session dependency.
models.py defines the SQLAlchemy tables Variety, Product, Batch, and StockMovement plus the Direction (IN/OUT) and TrackingType (weight/units) enums that drive stock behavior.
schemas.py provides Pydantic request/response models and enforces that BatchCreate and ProductDeduct supply a quantity (grams or units) via model_validator.
create_tables.py is a one-off bootstrap that runs Base.metadata.create_all against the configured engine to create the schema.
frontend/src/App.jsx is the dashboard: it polls /varieties and /batches, renders varieties and batches with expiry urgency, and runs the barcode scan flow.
frontend/src/RestockModal.jsx collects variety, quantity, and expiry inputs and POSTs a new batch to /batches.
frontend/src/DeductModal.jsx collects variety and quantity inputs and POSTs a manual removal to /deduct.
frontend/package.json defines the Vite/React toolchain scripts dev, build, lint (oxlint), and preview.

scripts/low_stock.py is a deterministic alert job: it sums OUT movements over the last 7 days, projects days-until-empty per variety, and emails low-stock warnings via SMTP using GMAIL_ADDRESS/GMAIL_PASSWORD; it is intended for scheduled/cron use, not the live request path.
.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml is a monthly scheduled GitHub Action that installs and runs `openwiki code --update` and opens a pull request to refresh the generated wiki.
AGENTS.md instructs agents to treat source code and tests as authoritative and to avoid hand-editing generated OpenWiki pages unless explicitly asked.
README.md provides the product summary, FIFO/expiry tracking explanation, local run instructions, and tech stack; CLAUDE.md points to AGENTS.md.
